Danté Exum keeping an 'open mind' about his role with the Utah Jazz this season|website=[[National Basketball Association|NBA.com]]|date=5 October 2019|accessdate=6 June 2024}} ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|d|ɑː|n|t|eɪ|_|ˈ|ɛ|k|s|ə|m}} {{respell|DAHN|tay|_|EK|səm}}; born 13 July 1995) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He chose to bypass college and was ultimately selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite magazine|last=Mannix|first=Chris|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2013/09/26/nba-draft-big-board-2014-andrew-wiggins|title=2014 NBA Big Board: Wiggins leads deepest draft in years|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=26 September 2013|access-date=2 December 2016}} Exum has played for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australia national team]] and won a bronze medal at the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Tokyo Olympics]]. ==Early career== Exum was born in the [[Melbourne]] suburb of [[East Melbourne, Victoria|East Melbourne]]{{cite web |title=Australia – 2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/9616/tid/239/_/2013_FIBA_U19_Championship_for_Men/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=30 December 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417214404/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/9616/tid/239/_/2013_FIBA_U19_Championship_for_Men/index.html |archive-date=17 April 2016}} to American parents. He played basketball for the Keilor Thunder as a junior{{cite web|last=D'Anello|first=Luke|url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/leader/west/former-keilor-thunder-basketballer-dante-exum-is-shooting-for-nba-selection/news-story/a7e856dcf7bb80d1e1e6770b2d5e57d6|title=Former Keilor Thunder basketballer Dante Exum is shooting for NBA selection|work=Herald Sun|date=19 November 2013|access-date=30 December 2024}} and also played [[Australian rules football]] at school.{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-06-27/nba-not-afl-was-the-way-to-go-dante-exum/5554004|title=NBA Draft: Dante Exum happy with decision to play basketball over AFL|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|date=27 June 2014|access-date=27 June 2014}} He attended [[Thomas Carr College]] in Melbourne.{{cite news |last1=Capone |first1=Alesha |title=Olympic fever at Tarneit school |url=https://wyndham.starweekly.com.au/news/olympic-fever-at-tarneit-school/ |access-date=30 December 2024 |work=starweekly.com.au |publisher=Wyndham |date=4 August 2021}} He later moved to [[Canberra]] to attend the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] and [[UC Senior Secondary College Lake Ginninderra|Lake Ginninderra Secondary College]]. He competed for Lake Ginninderra in the Australian National High School Basketball Championships in 2013,{{cite web|url=http://www.basketball.net.au/exum-headlines-2013-australian-school-cships/|title=EXUM HEADLINES 2013 AUSTRALIAN SCHOOL C'SHIPS|work=Basketball.net.au|date=1 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2016|archive-date=2 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202171129/http://www.basketball.net.au/exum-headlines-2013-australian-school-cships/|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|last=Smart|first=Nick|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/basketball/australian-young-gun-dante-exum-focus-of-attention-at-australian-school-champs/story-fni2u9cl-1226773638407|title=Australian young gun Dante Exum focus of attention at Australian School Champs|work=Herald Sun|date=2 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2013}} helping them win the title.{{cite web|url=http://www.basketball.net.au/rowville-and-lake-ginninderra-win-asc-titles/|title=ROWVILLE AND LAKE GINNINDERRA WIN ASC TITLES|work=Basketball.net.au|date=6 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2016|archive-date=3 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161203060422/http://www.basketball.net.au/rowville-and-lake-ginninderra-win-asc-titles/|url-status=dead}} In April 2013, Exum participated in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] for the World Select Team, where he recorded 16 points, three rebounds and two assists in a 112–98 win over the USA Junior Select Team.{{cite web|last=Kamalsky|first=Matt|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2013-Nike-Hoop-Summit-Game-Recap-4149/|title=2013 Nike Hoop Summit Game Recap|work=DraftExpress.com|date=21 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140803152823/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2013-Nike-Hoop-Summit-Game-Recap-4149/|url-status=dead}} In October 2013, Exum graduated from high school in Australia and had the option to enroll in college and play [[college basketball]] during the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], but he decided against it.{{cite web|last=Goodman|first=Jeff|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9609453/dante-exum-enroll-college-december|title=Dante Exum undecided on college|publisher=ESPN|date=28 August 2013|access-date=28 August 2013}} On 28 January 2014, it was announced that Exum signed with agents from Landmark Sports and that he would declare for the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last=Ford|first=Chad|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10363177/dante-exum-declares-2014-nba-draft|title=Dante Exum declares for draft|publisher=ESPN|date=28 January 2014|access-date=2 December 2016}}{{cite web |date=29 January 2014 |title=Australian teen Dante Exum set for NBA draft |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/basketball/australian-teen-dante-exum-set-for-nba-draft/news-story/b02eab1d12093cf6f9b0ab89d91c16b1 |access-date=29 January 2014 |work=Herald Sun}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2014–2019)=== [[File:Dante Exum Utah (cropped).jpg|upright=0.85|thumb|Exum with the Utah Jazz in 2018]] Exum was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-selects-exum-hood-2014-nba-draft|title=Jazz Selects Exum, Hood in 2014 NBA Draft|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=26 June 2014|access-date=26 June 2014}} He made his NBA debut in the Jazz's season opener on 29 October, scoring five points in 9½ minutes off the bench in a 104–93 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/HOUUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets spoil Snyder's NBA coaching debut|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=29 October 2014|access-date=29 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225010745/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/HOUUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=25 December 2014|url-status=dead}} On 22 January, he scored a career-high 15 points on five 3-pointers in a 101–99 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150122/UTAMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Hayward scores 24, Jazz hold on for 101–99 win over Bucks|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=22 January 2015|access-date=22 January 2015}} On 1 April, he had a career-high 12 assists in a 98–84 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150401/DENUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Jazz roll Nuggets 98–84 after sluggish start|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=2 December 2015|access-date=1 April 2015}} He appeared in all 82 games (41 starts) as a rookie and averaged 4.8 points, 1.6 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 22.2 minutes. Exum became only the 10th rookie in Jazz history to play in all 82 games, scoring in double figures in 13 games and leading the team in assists 11 times. He helped the Jazz to a 24–17 record as a starter and was selected to compete in the 2015 Rising Stars Challenge during the [[2015 NBA All-Star Game|NBA's All-Star Weekend]] in New York.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-exercise-team-options-four-players|title=Jazz Exercise Team Options on Four Players|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=17 October 2015|access-date=17 October 2015}} In August 2015, Exum sustained a tear of the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) in his left knee while playing for Australia in Slovenia.{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/acl-injury-could-rule-out-dante-exum-for-entire-nba-season-with-utah-jazz-reports/news-story/6ce62f6966677125deca39e8a8f8c600|title=NBA: Utah Jazz teammate Joe Ingles backs Dante Exum after reports of season-ending ACL injury|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=5 August 2015|access-date=5 August 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/dante-exum-injury-update-august-6-2015|title=Danté Exum Injury Update (August 6, 2015)|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=6 August 2015|access-date=6 August 2015}} He underwent surgery and subsequently missed the entire 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/dante-exum-injury-update|title=Danté Exum Injury Update|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=3 September 2015|access-date=3 September 2015}} Exum returned to action in the 2016–17 season. He played in 28 of the first 29 games of the season, but then sat out 10 of 11 games between 21 December and 10 January.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/exumda01/gamelog/2017/|title=Dante Exum 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=28 December 2018}} On 11 March, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 112–104 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900368|title=Westbrook has another triple-double, Thunder beat Jazz|publisher=ESPN|date=11 March 2017|access-date=11 March 2017}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/watch-exum-scores-career-high-22-points-in-loss-to-okc/11xa1jx0wipbn1r1ie8nwnrr4z|title=WATCH: Exum scores career-high 22 points in loss to OKC|work=SportingNews.com|date=11 March 2017|access-date=28 December 2018}} In October 2017, Exum underwent shoulder surgery.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975773|title=Mitchell, Gobert lead Jazz over Suns for 8th straight win|publisher=ESPN|date=15 March 2018|access-date=15 March 2018}} He made his first appearance of the season on 15 March 2018, finishing with 10 points in a 116–88 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On 30 March 2018, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 107–97 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975881|title=Mitchell, Exum lead Jazz past Grizzlies, 107–97|publisher=ESPN|date=30 March 2018|access-date=30 March 2018}} On 6 July 2018, Exum re-signed with the Jazz.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-agree-terms-favors-exum-and-neto|title=Jazz Agree to Terms with Favors, Exum and Neto|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=6 July 2018|access-date=6 July 2018}} On 27 December 2018, he scored a season-high 20 points in a 114–97 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071191|title=Redick scores 24, Embiid has 23, 76ers roll over Jazz 114–97|publisher=ESPN|date=27 December 2018|access-date=28 December 2018}} Two days later, in his first start of the season, Exum had 13 points and a career-high 13 assists in a 129–97 victory over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071208|title=Gobert leads Jazz past Knicks 129–97|publisher=ESPN|date=29 December 2018|access-date=30 December 2018}} On 7 January 2019, he was ruled out for "a couple of weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered two days earlier against the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|last=Irving|first=Kyle|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/nba/news/dante-exum-utah-jazz-sprained-ankle-miss-couple-of-weeks/xxjpf0xj41541a27eg8f2t82u|title=Report: Dante Exum expected to miss 'a couple of weeks' with sprained ankle|work=SportingNews.com|date=7 January 2019|access-date=8 January 2019}} His return was delayed after developing a bone bruise from his ankle sprain.{{cite web|last=Griffin|first=Taylor|url=https://www.slcdunk.com/the-downbeat-latest-jazz-news/2019/2/28/18244021/raul-neto-utah-jazz-important-ricky-rubio-dante-exum-injury|title=Raul Neto is more important than you think|work=slcdunk.com|date=28 February 2019|access-date=28 February 2019}} He returned to action on 11 March against the Thunder after missing 25 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071678|title=Thunder beat Jazz 98–89 to sweep season series|publisher=ESPN|date=11 March 2019|access-date=12 March 2019}} Four days later however, he was ruled out indefinitely after sustaining a partially torn patellar tendon in his right knee.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/dante-exum-injury-update-3152019|title=Danté Exum injury update—3.15.2019|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=15 March 2019|access-date=15 March 2019}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2019–2021)=== On 24 December 2019, Exum was traded, alongside two second-round picks, to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Jordan Clarkson]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/exum-trade-191224|title=Cavs Acquire Dante Exum and Two Draft Picks from Utah|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=24 December 2019|access-date=24 December 2019}} On 16 January 2021, Exum was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in a multi-player, four-team deal with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] that sent [[James Harden]] to the [[Brooklyn Nets]]; the Cavaliers received [[Taurean Prince]] and [[Jarrett Allen]] in the deal.{{cite web|title=Rockets Announce Revised Four-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-revised-four-team-trade|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=16 January 2021|access-date=17 January 2021}} He did not appear in any regular season games for Houston, although he did play sparse minutes in the preseason for the Rockets. On 17 September 2021, Exum re-signed with the Rockets.{{cite web|title=Rockets Re-sign Danté Exum|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-dante-exum|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=17 September 2021|access-date=19 September 2021}} However, he was waived on 16 October.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Rockets Waive Dante Exum|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/rockets-waive-dante-exum.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=16 October 2021|access-date=31 October 2021}} ===FC Barcelona (2021–2022)=== On 7 December 2021, Exum signed with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Dante Exum, a reinforcement for the perimeter|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/2399021/dante-exum-a-reinforcement-for-the-perimeter|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=7 December 2021|access-date=7 December 2021}} ===Partizan Belgrade (2022–2023)=== On 10 July 2022, Exum signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=Dante Egzum je novi košarkaš Partizana NIS |url=https://kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest/3260/dante-egzum-je-novi-kosarkas-partizana-nis |access-date=10 July 2022 |website=kkpartizan.rs |language=en}} During the 2022–23 season, Partizan was eliminated by [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the [[2023 EuroLeague Playoffs|playoffs]]. Over the season, Exum averaged 13.2 points, 2.7 assists and 2.3 rebounds per game. Partizan ended the 2022–23 season by lifting the [[2022–23 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship trophy, after 3–2 score against [[Red Star Belgrade|Crvena zvezda]] in the Finals series.{{cite news |title=PARTIZAN MOZZART BET ARE 2022/23 ADMIRALBET ABA LEAGUE CHAMPIONS |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/49109/partizan-mozzart-bet-are-2022-23-admiralbet-aba-league-champions/ |access-date=23 June 2023 |work=aba-liga.com |date=22 June 2023}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2026)=== On 14 July 2023, Exum signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |title=Mavericks add veteran guard Exum|url=https://www.mavs.com/exum-signs/|date=14 July 2023|access-date=14 July 2023|website=mavs.com}} He made his debut for the Mavericks on 25 October in a 126–119 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584701|title=Mavericks spoil Victor Wembanyama's NBA debut, beat the Spurs 126–119 in the teams' opener|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=25 October 2023|access-date=25 October 2023}} On 12 December, Exum scored a season-high 26 points with a career-high seven made three-pointers in a 127–125 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dante-exum-career-night-dallas-mavs-thrilling-win-los-angeles-lakers|title=Dante Exum Has Career Night in Dallas Mavs' Thrilling Win Over Los Angeles Lakers: 'Left Me Wide-Open'|publisher=si.com|date=12 December 2023|accessdate=31 December 2023}} In 55 games (17 starts) for the team, he averaged 7.8 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 2.9 assists. Exum helped the Mavericks reach the [[2024 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] where they lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|publisher=cbsnews.com|access-date=17 June 2024|date=17 June 2024}} Exum made 18 appearances (12 starts) during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.1 points, 1.7 assists, and 2.8 assists. On 14 March 2025, he was ruled out for the remainder of the season after suffering a broken bone in his left hand during a game against the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web|title=Dante Exum breaks bone in hand as Mavericks' woes worsen|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44256935/sources-exum-breaks-bone-hand-mavericks-woes-worsen|access-date=4 April 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} On 2 September 2025, he re-signed with the Mavericks on a one-year contract.{{Cite web |date=2 September 2025|title=Mavs re-sign Dante Exum|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-re-sign-dante-exum/|access-date=2 September 2025|website=mavs.com}} On 20 November, before playing in any games during the season, Exum was ruled out for the remainder of the season to undergo surgery on his right knee.{{Cite web|title=Mavs' Dante Exum to undergo season-ending knee surgery|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47038896/mavs-dante-exum-undergo-season-ending-knee-surgery|date=November 20, 2025|website=espn.com}} On 5 February 2026, Exum was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-10-time-all-star-anthony-davis|title=Wizards Acquire 10-Time All-Star Anthony Davis |work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}} Three days later, Exum was waived by Washington.{{cite web |title=Dante Exum waived by Wizards |url=https://basketnews.com/news-240816-dante-exum-waived-by-wizards.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=9 February Zealand]] at the [[2013 FIBA Oceania Championship]]. In 2014, he played for Australia at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 FIBA World Cup]], where he averaged 2.7 points, 1.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists in six games.{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Dante-Exum|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140901172532/http://www.fiba.com/basketballworldcup/2014/Dante-EXUM|url-status=live|archive-date=1
